The Project

Named for a tree, shaped like a curve

The Khaya is a hardwood the developer takes as its symbol — strength, elegance, and shade. The building answers it with a form the brochure calls a flowing masterpiece: a 61-storey tower that curves as it rises, its lower flank stepping down in terraces towards the podium.

That curve is what makes the amenity unusual. Instead of one deck, Khaya has two — a garden level at Level 8 carrying fifty numbered facilities, and a pair of floors at the very top: a Sky Gym on Level 60 and a Sky Lawn on Level 61. Between them sit 795 serviced apartments, and the upper floors are made almost entirely of one-off layouts — twenty "X" types, two units of each.

It is built by Bayu Mantap Sdn Bhd, a member of the Melati Ehsan Group, in collaboration with Tenaga Nasional Berhad — and the sales gallery sits inside Menara TNB Bangsar.

Why Khaya

Eight things that actually separate it

All drawn from the developer's own e-brochure and its advertising permit.

01

A lawn at Level 61

A Sky Lawn on the 61st floor and a Sky Gym on the 60th — amenity at the very top of the tower, not only at its base.

02

Fifty facilities on Level 8

The Hub numbers fifty items across indoor and outdoor: pickleball court, home theatre, music room, sauna, three cabanas and two dining pavilions with jacuzzis.

03

A 50 m infinity lap pool

A full fifty-metre lap length on the garden deck — not a plunge pool with a view.

04

Twenty bespoke upper types

Above the standard floors sit twenty "X" layouts, two units of each, from 857 up to 2,427 sq ft. The top of the tower is effectively made to order.

05

A Bangsar address

Between Kuala Lumpur and Bangsar, with LRT Abdullah Hukum and Kerinchi close by and KL Eco City, Mid Valley and Bangsar Village within the neighbourhood.

06

Built with TNB

Melati Ehsan Group in collaboration with Tenaga Nasional Berhad, Malaysia's national electricity utility. The sales gallery is inside Menara TNB Bangsar.

07

A curve, not a slab

The tower's flowing form steps down in terraces on one flank — which is what creates the sky floors and the terraces on the upper types.

08

Provisional GreenRE

Certified provisionally under GreenRE, with multi-tiered security and lush landscaping through the podium levels.

The Architectural Concept

Two decks, fifty-two floors apart

Most towers give you one amenity level. Khaya's curve creates two — and they are built for completely different halves of a day.

61

Sky Lawn

Level 61

A lawn on the roof. The brochure's line for it is "Soar above the city on the 61st floor" — as you ascend, the city quiets.

60

Sky Deck

Level 60

The Horizon Gym and a green rooftop deck — a gym with the skyline through floor-to-ceiling glass on both sides.

Before You Ask

The questions that come up first

In Bangsar, Kuala Lumpur — the brochure places it between Kuala Lumpur and Bangsar, near the TNB landholding off Jalan Pantai Baharu, with the Federal Highway, NPE, Sprint and Salak Expressway around it and LRT Abdullah Hukum and Kerinchi closest. The sales gallery is inside Menara TNB Bangsar, No. 170 Jalan Bangsar. The brochure maps the neighbourhood but publishes no distances, so none are quoted on this page — ask me and I'll send measured times.

Prices move with the stock that is left and with whatever launch package is running, so this page deliberately doesn't print a figure — and the spread here is wide, because it runs from the smallest standard type all the way to a bespoke X type. Message me and I'll send the current price list for the layout, floor and facing you're weighing up.

Level 60 is the Sky Deck — the Horizon Gym plus a green rooftop deck. Level 61 is the Sky Lawn, an open lawn at the top of the tower. They are separate from the main amenity floor: Level 8, The Hub, which numbers fifty facilities including a 50 m infinity lap pool, a pickleball court, a home theatre, a music room, saunas, three cabanas and two dining pavilions with jacuzzis.

Leasehold, 99 years, expiring 12 June 2117 — roughly 91 years still to run. There is a restriction in interest (the land cannot be transferred, leased or charged without the consent of the Federal Territory Land Executive Committee), and the permit records no encumbrance on the land.

795 serviced apartments over 61 storeys. Fifteen standard types run from 630 sq ft (Type B) to 1,321 sq ft (Type L), and above them sit twenty bespoke "X" types with two units of each — X17 at 2,427 sq ft down to X30 at 857 sq ft. Type A is the most common by a wide margin at 181 units; Type B follows at 100.

The expected date of completion on the advertising permit is June 2029.

Bayu Mantap Sdn Bhd (201101037126 / 965260-D), a member of the Melati Ehsan Group, at No. 5 Jalan Titiwangsa, 53200 Kuala Lumpur. The brochure states the project is brought forward in collaboration with Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB), Malaysia's national electricity utility. Developer's Licence 30531/08-2028/0208(N), valid 16/08/2023 to 15/08/2028; approved by DBKL.

Good catch, and worth being straight about. For three types the brochure's floor-plan pages and its advertising permit disagree slightly: Type G (plan 1,086 sq ft / permit 1,095), Type H (plan 1,028 / permit 1,032) and Type I (plan 1,096 / permit 1,057). This page quotes the permit figures, because that is the legally lodged document. Confirm the exact built-up for your specific unit in the Sale and Purchase Agreement.

Several types — A, D, F, H, I and the X range — come with an air-conditioner ledge of 32.29 sq ft recorded as an accessory parcel. It is additional to the built-up area quoted, and it belongs to your unit rather than to the common property.

Yes — the sales gallery is at G-06, Menara TNB Bangsar, No. 170 Jalan Bangsar, 59200 Kuala Lumpur. Send me your preferred day and time on WhatsApp and I'll arrange it and meet you there.
